question: What is the primary mode of transmission for Mycobacterium tuberculosis?

options.C: Direct contact with contaminated skin wounds

explanation: TB bacteria spread through the air when a person with active disease coughs or sneezes, allowing others to inhale the droplets into their lungs. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h1)

question: What does a positive Mantoux test result primarily indicate?

options.A: Immunity acquired from a recent bacterial cold
options.C: The presence of active, contagious lung disease
options.D: Exposure to the tuberculosis bacterium in the past

explanation: The TST only shows that the body's immune system has encountered the TB bacteria, creating a hypersensitivity reaction, but it cannot tell if the infection is active or dormant. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h1)

question: What type of immune reaction causes the raised bump during a Mantoux test?
explanation: Think of this as your immune cells (T-cells) rushing to the spot and throwing a little party that takes a day or two to show up as a firm lump! [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h2)

question: Why must a patient return 48 to 72 hours after getting a Mantoux injection?

options.A: To ensure the PPD liquid does not leak out of the skin layers
options.B: To receive a second booster dose in the exact same location
options.C: To allow enough time for the delayed immune reaction to peak
options.D: To prevent the injection site from becoming infected with bacteria

explanation: The cellular immune response takes two to three days to build enough local induration to be accurately measured by a healthcare provider. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h2)

question: What is the standard dose of PPD administered during a Mantoux test?
explanation: The standard diagnostic dose for standard PPD screening is exactly 0.1 mL, which equals 5 tuberculin units. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h3)

question: Which syringe and needle setup is best for giving a Mantoux skin test?

options.A: A 1-mL tuberculin syringe with a short 27-gauge fine needle
options.B: A 5-mL syringe with a blunt-tip drawing needle
options.C: An insulin syringe marked in units with a permanent attached needle
options.D: A 3-mL syringe with a large 21-gauge intramuscular needle

explanation: You need a tiny syringe to measure tiny drops accurately, and a short, fine needle helps you slide the fluid right into the top layers of the skin! [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h3)

question: What visual sign immediately confirms a successful intradermal PPD injection?

options.A: A flat red rash spreading on the arm
options.B: A small droplet of bright red blood
options.D: A pale raised skin bleb or wheal

explanation: A proper intradermal injection creates a distinct bump or wheal on the skin surface, showing the fluid is trapped in the correct layer. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h4)

question: What should you do right after pulling the needle out of a PPD injection site?

options.A: Pat the area gently with cotton without rubbing it
options.B: Massage the skin vigorously to help absorb the fluid
options.C: Apply a tight pressure bandage to stop any bleeding
options.D: Clean the skin again with a fresh alcohol swab

explanation: Hands off that bubble! Rubbing or massaging can push the fluid away or mess up the skin test results. Just a gentle dab if needed. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h4)

question: When reading a Mantoux test, what part of the skin reaction do you actually measure?

options.A: The hard, raised area of tissue known as induration
options.B: The dark bruising caused by the needle puncture
options.C: The total diameter of visible surface redness
options.D: The size of the initial wheal left after the injection

explanation: Don't measure the redness! Feel for the edges of that firm, hard bump underneath (the induration)—that's what tells the real story. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h5)

question: What should you do if your patient shows up for their Mantoux reading at 96 hours (4 days) instead of 72 hours?

options.A: Measure the induration carefully and record it as normal
options.B: Document the reading as positive due to delayed reaction
options.C: Consult a physician to prescribe prophylactic antibiotics
options.D: Consider the test invalid and schedule a repeat screening

explanation: Time is key! After 72 hours, the immune reaction starts fading away, making the results unreliable. It's best to repeat the test. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h5)

question: Which induration measurement is considered positive for a patient with no known risk factors for tuberculosis?
explanation: For healthy individuals with no known exposure risks, the cut-off threshold for a positive test is 15 millimeters or greater. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h6)

question: Why is a smaller bump size (5 mm) counted as positive for patients living with HIV?

options.A: They are more likely to have allergic reactions to the PPD liquid
options.B: They process the antigen much faster than healthy people
options.C: Their weakened immune systems cannot produce large inflammatory lumps
options.D: Their skin is thinner and harder to measure accurately

explanation: Because their immune systems are fighting harder battles, they can't throw a massive inflammatory response. So, even a smaller firm bump is a big red flag we take seriously! [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h6)

question: What is a frequent cause of a false-positive Mantoux test in individuals from other countries?

options.A: Prior vaccination with the BCG vaccine
options.B: Having a severe viral cold during testing
options.C: Receiving the injection too deep in the skin

explanation: The BCG vaccine, given in many countries to prevent childhood TB, can cause the immune system to react to PPD, creating a false-positive skin test. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h7)

question: Which factor can cause a false-negative Mantoux result in someone who actually has TB?

options.A: Receiving a fresh dose of the PPD antigen
options.B: Reading the test exactly at 48 hours
options.D: Having a history of latent tuberculosis infection

explanation: If the immune system is deeply suppressed, it might not put up any fight at all, leaving you with a blank (false-negative) skin test even if TB is present. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h7)

question: What instructions should a nurse give a patient regarding care of the Mantoux injection site?

options.A: Massage ointment into the skin to reduce swelling
options.B: Keep the area clean, dry, and uncovered without scratching
options.C: Apply a medicated adhesive bandage over the bleb immediately
options.D: Wash the site vigorously with hot soapy water twice a day

explanation: Patients should leave the site alone, avoiding scratching or covering it, to ensure the local skin reaction remains undisturbed until it is read. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h8)

question: What is the best next step for a patient who comes back with a strongly positive Mantoux test?

options.A: Discharge the patient with instructions to return next year
options.B: Refer the patient for a chest X-ray and clinical evaluation
options.C: Immediately start a full course of multi-drug TB treatment
options.D: Administer a second booster Mantoux test on the other arm

explanation: A positive skin test is a warning sign, not a final diagnosis. We always send them for a chest X-ray to check if their lungs are clear or if the infection is active. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h8)
